questions.prompt: Complete the polite request: "Could you ___ me the way to the station, please?"
questions.explanation: "Could you" is followed by the bare verb, with no "to" and no -ing: Could you show me the way to the station? "showing" belongs after "Would you mind", not after "Could you"; "to show" and "shows" are not the bare verb.

questions.prompt: Your friend is about to touch a hot pan. Which warning is correct?
questions.explanation: To warn, "Mind" is followed directly by the noun phrase that names the danger: Mind the pan! "Mind to" and "Mind of" add a preposition copied from "pay attention to"; "Minding" is not an imperative, so it cannot give a warning.

questions.prompt: A sign on a laboratory door forbids touching the chemicals. Which sign is correct?
questions.explanation: A sign forbids with "Don't" + the bare verb: Don't touch! "Not touch" drops "do"; "Don't to touch" and "Don't touching" add "to" or -ing, which never come after "Don't".

questions.prompt: The receptionist says: "I'll carry your bags to your room." Which answer thanks her correctly?

options.text: That will be very kind for you.
That will be very kind of you.
That will be very kind to you.

questions.explanation: The help is still to come, so "That will be", and the kindness belongs to her, so "kind of you": That will be very kind of you. "kind for you" and "kind to you" use the wrong preposition; "You're welcome" is the answer TO thanks, not a thank-you.

questions.prompt: A tourist looks lost in the street. Which sentence is NOT an offer of help?

options.text: Could you show me the way, please?
What can I do to help you find your way?

questions.explanation: "Could you show me the way, please?" is a polite request: the speaker asks the OTHER person to help, so it is not an offer — and it is the tourist, not you, who would say it. The three other sentences are offers, because the speaker is the helper: Do you need any help? / How can I help you? / What can I do to help you find your way?

options.text: Could you clean the floor, please?
Do you need any help with the floor?
Look out! The floor is wet.

questions.explanation: "Look out!" is the warning cry, and the sentence after it names the danger: Look out! The floor is wet. "Could you clean…?" is a polite request, "What about cleaning…?" is a suggestion, and "Do you need any help…?" offers help.
